# Metrics & KPI Definition

## Overview

This document defines measurable metrics and targets for evaluating playbook effectiveness, output quality, and domain outcomes.

---

## 1. Process Metrics

Process metrics measure how efficiently the playbook guides the workflow.

### 1.1 Phase Completion Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Phases completed first attempt | ≥85% | Count phases that pass gate on first try |
| Average iterations per phase | ≤1.5 | Count gate retries / total phases |
| Phase duration accuracy | ±25% | (Actual - Estimated) / Estimated |
| Gate verification time | ≤10 min | Time from gate start to PASS |

### 1.2 Task Execution Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Tasks completed per session | 5-15 | Count tasks marked complete per session |
| Task rollback rate | ≤10% | Tasks that required undo / total tasks |
| Blocker resolution time | <30 min avg | Time from blocker identified to resolved |
| Escalation rate | ≤20% | Escalated tasks / total tasks |

### 1.3 Context Efficiency Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Context load time | <30 sec | Time to load phase context |
| Token usage per phase | Within budget | Compare to context_budget setting |
| Context carry accuracy | 100% | decisions-ledger completeness check |

### 1.4 Session Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Session completion rate | 100% | Phases complete in planned session |
| Context loss incidents | 0 | Count sessions that lost context |
| Handoff success rate | 100% | Successful phase transitions / total transitions |

---

## 2. Quality Metrics

Quality metrics measure the correctness and completeness of outputs.

### 2.1 Specification Quality (Phase 0-1)

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Purpose statement clarity | 1 paragraph, unambiguous | Human review |
| Scope completeness | All in/out/adjacent defined | Checklist audit |
| Success criteria measurability | 100% measurable | Each criterion has metric |
| Technical constraints coverage | All documented | Checklist audit |

### 2.2 Architecture Quality (Phase 2)

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Requirement coverage | 100% | Every spec requirement has task |
| Formula boundary verification | 100% | All formulas tested at param=0, param=1 |
| Buffer size coverage | 192kHz compatible | All buffer calculations verified |
| Cross-cutting concern coverage | All addressed | CCC mapping complete |

### 2.3 Implementation Quality (Phase 4-7)

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Build success rate | 100% | cmake --build succeeds |
| Test pass rate | 100% | ctest passes |
| Parameter smoothing coverage | 100% | All modulatable parameters smoothed |
| Audio thread safety | 100% | No allocations in processBlock |
| GUI accessibility | Tab navigation works | Keyboard-only navigation test |

### 2.4 Validation Quality (Phase 8-9)

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Unit test coverage | ≥80% lines | Coverage tool output |
| pluginval validation | Pass | pluginval --strict passes |
| Gain staging verification | No clips, no silence | -60dB to 0dB range verified |
| Human perceptual approval | 100% | Human signs off on sound |

### 2.5 Release Quality (Phase 10-13)

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| License system reliability | 100% | All license checks work |
| Marketplace listing completeness | All fields populated | Checklist audit |
| Distribution package integrity | All platforms tested | Build and load tests |

---

## 3. Domain Outcome Metrics

Domain metrics measure the effectiveness of the final plugin product.

### 3.1 Audio Quality Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| CPU usage | ≤5% at 48kHz/512 buffer | DAW CPU meter |
| Memory footprint | ≤50MB baseline | Process memory in DAW |
| Latency | ≤1ms additional | Reported latency |
| Sample rate support | 44.1kHz to 192kHz | All rates tested |

### 3.2 User Experience Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| GUI responsiveness | <16ms response time | Interaction timing |
| Preset load time | <500ms | File timing |
| Parameter automation | Click-free | Audio analysis |
| Plugin load time | <2 seconds | DAW scan time |

### 3.3 Commercial Metrics (Phase 10-13)

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Marketplace approval rate | 100% | All marketplaces approve |
| Customer support tickets | ≤5 per 100 sales | Support tracking |
| Documentation completeness | All sections filled | Checklist audit |
| Pricing accuracy | Correct on all platforms | Cross-platform check |

### 3.4 Maintenance Metrics (Phase 15-16)

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Bug report resolution time | ≤7 days | Time from report to fix |
| KB update frequency | Per run | KB entries updated after run |
| Playbook version currency | Latest | Version matches repo |

---

## 4. Knowledge Base Metrics

KB metrics measure knowledge base effectiveness.

### 4.1 KB Quality Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Entry schema compliance | 100% | All entries pass validation |
| Bridge mapping accuracy | Verified per use | Parameter ranges tested |
| Cross-reference validity | 100% | All references resolve |
| Authority score accuracy | Documented | Confidence scores justified |

### 4.2 KB Usage Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| KB layer load accuracy | Per phase mapping | Only required layers loaded |
| Bridge lookup success | 100% | All creative terms translate |
| Reference hit rate | ≥80% | Referenced entries / accessed entries |
| Placeholder resolution | Before use | All placeholders resolved |

---

## 5. Cross-Cutting Concern Metrics

Each CCC has specific quality targets.

| CCC | Metric | Target |
|-----|--------|--------|
| Real-Time Safety | Audio thread allocations | 0 |
| Gain Staging | Headroom margin | ≥6dB at each stage |
| Parameter Safety | Clicks on automation | 0 |
| Preset Integrity | Preset load success | 100% |
| GUI Responsiveness | Response time | <16ms |
| Cross-Platform | Platform-specific bugs | 0 |
| DAW Compatibility | Compatibility failures | 0 |
| Performance Profiling | CPU spikes | <10% above baseline |
| Security | Vulnerabilities | 0 critical |
| Reproducibility | Build reproducibility | 100% |

---

## 6. Metrics Collection Protocol

### When to Record

| Phase | Metrics Recorded |
|-------|------------------|
| 0-1 | Specification quality metrics |
| 2 | Architecture quality metrics |
| 3 | Build setup metrics |
| 4-7 | Implementation quality metrics |
| 8-9 | Validation quality metrics |
| 10-13 | Commercial, release quality metrics |
| 14-15 | Maintenance metrics |
| 16 | KB metrics |

### How to Record

1. **Phase Gate:** Record phase metrics in metrics-tracker.md
2. **Task Completion:** Record task metrics in decisions-ledger
3. **Quality Gates:** Record quality metrics at each gate
4. **Final Review:** Aggregate metrics in post-run review

### Metrics Storage

- **metrics-tracker.md** — Running metrics log
- **decisions-ledger.md** — Phase-by-phase decisions with metrics
- **post-run-review.md** — Final aggregated metrics (created at Phase 15)

---

## 7. KPI Targets Summary

### Primary KPIs (Must Meet)

| KPI | Target | Consequence if Missed |
|-----|--------|----------------------|
| Gate pass rate (first attempt) | ≥85% | Review phase structure |
| Build success rate | 100% | Block release |
| Test pass rate | 100% | Block release |
| Audio thread safety | 100% | Block release |
| Human approval | 100% | Block phase progression |

### Secondary KPIs (Should Meet)

| KPI | Target | Consequence if Missed |
|-----|--------|----------------------|
| Phase duration accuracy | ±25% | Update estimates |
| KB entry compliance | 100% | Fix before use |
| Bridge mapping accuracy | 100% | Review translations |

### Tertiary KPIs (Nice to Have)

| KPI | Target | Consequence if Missed |
|-----|--------|----------------------|
| CPU usage | ≤5% | Optimize if exceeded |
| Session completion rate | 100% | Review session breaks |
| Escalation rate | ≤20% | Review blocker patterns |

---

## 8. Metrics Review Cadence

| Timing | Review Type | Participants |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| Each phase gate | Gate metrics | [Coordinator], [Human] if approval |
| End of session | Session metrics | [Coordinator] |
| End of run | Post-run review | [Coordinator], [Human] |
| Continuous improvement | KB metrics | [Coordinator] |

---

## 9. Escalation Triggers

Metrics that trigger immediate escalation:

| Metric | Threshold | Escalation |
|--------|-----------|------------|
| Build failure | Any | Immediate escalation to [Human] |
| Test failure | Any | 30-minute self-attempt, then escalate |
| Audio thread allocation | Any | Immediate escalation to [Human] |
| Human approval rejected | Any | Immediate — human already engaged |
| Gate fail after 3 attempts | 3 | Escalate with options documented |

---

## 10. Success Criteria

Phase 8 is complete when:

- [x] Process metrics defined with targets
- [x] Quality metrics defined with targets
- [x] Domain outcome metrics defined with targets
- [x] KB metrics defined with targets
- [x] Cross-cutting concern metrics defined
- [x] Metrics collection protocol defined
- [x] KPI targets established (primary, secondary, tertiary)
- [x] Escalation triggers defined

- Developing product concept from commission brief
- Creating specification from research
- Analyzing improvement opportunities

**writing-plans** — Used to create implementation plans from specifications. Activates when:
- Translating approved specification into actionable tasks
- Designing architecture from requirements
- Breaking down complex phases into executable steps

**execute-plans** — Primary execution skill. Used for implementing plans with a single agent. Activates when:
- Executing tasks from an approved implementation plan
- Following step-by-step instructions
- Completing implementation phases sequentially
- **Preferred method for most phases**

**sub-agent driven development** — Alternative execution method using multiple specialized sub-agents. Use when:
- Complex multi-component development requiring parallel work
- Large-scale refactoring requiring coordinated changes
- Multiple independent systems need simultaneous development
- **Use sparingly — execute-plans is preferred for single-agent workflow**

```
    ↓

```

2. **writing-plans unavailable** → Proceed with manual architecture design
3. **execute-plans unavailable** → Execute tasks directly with single agent
4. **sub-agent unavailable** → Always fallback to execute-plans

# Output Configuration

## Overview

This document defines how the JUCE VST Business Playbook operates: workflow model, usage instructions, KB mapping, skill activation, and post-run review.

---

## 1. Workflow Model

### Model: Human-in-the-Loop

**Justification:** 
- Creative decisions (sound identity, GUI aesthetic, preset names) require human judgment
- Perceptual testing (DAW testing, sound quality) requires human ears
- Business decisions (pricing, marketing, launch timing) require human approval
- AI handles implementation, research, and synthesis — human directs

### Role Definitions (Condensed for JSON)

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "Human": {
      "description": "Creative director, final decision-maker, perceptual tester",
      "decision_authority": "exclusive on creative decisions, approval on all gates",
      "appears_in_phases": [0, 1, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13]
    },
    "Coordinator": {
      "description": "Process manager, gate verification, status tracking",
      "decision_authority": "gate PASS/FAIL, escalation routing",
      "appears_in_phases": "all"
    },
    "Builder": {
      "description": "Code implementation, testing, building",
      "decision_authority": "implementation details within approved architecture",
      "appears_in_phases": [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13]
    },
    "Architect": {
      "description": "Design, planning, architecture",
      "decision_authority": "architecture design within approved scope",
      "appears_in_phases": [2, 4, 5, 6]
    }
  }
}
```

### Single-Agent Mapping

When executed by one AI agent:
- Agent fills: [Coordinator], [Builder], [Architect]
- Human fills: [Human]
- Agent switches mindset based on task owner

---

## 2. Usage Instructions

### How to Start

**Initial Context Required:**
1. Commission brief: What plugin to build (type, sound identity, constraints)
2. Technical constraints: JUCE version, formats, platforms
3. Creative direction: Sound identity in user's exact words (no AI paraphrasing)

**First Session Loads:**
- Commission brief (user provides)
- This playbook (phases, tasks, gates)
- KB layers: None for Phase 0-1, Technical for Phase 2+

**Example Start Prompt:**
```
I want to build a [synthesizer/effect/plugin type] called [name].
The sound should be [user's exact words: warm, lush, aggressive, etc].
Technical constraints: JUCE 8.0.x, VST3, Linux primary, $200/month budget.
[More details from commission brief]
```

### Session Strategy

**Session Breaks (Recommended):**

| Session | Phases | Reason |
|---------|--------|--------|
| 1 | 0-1 | Commission, Research (creative decisions) |
| 2 | 2-3 | KB Architecture, Bootstrapping (knowledge structure) |
| 3 | 4-5 | DSP, State Management (heavy implementation) |
| 4 | 6-7 | Integration, GUI (more implementation) |
| 5 | 8-9 | Validation, DAW Testing (requires working plugin) |
| 6 | 10-12 | Licensing, Marketplace, Marketing (commercial) |
| 7 | 13-16 | Release, Post-Launch, Improvement, KB Maintenance |

**Session Context Carry:**
- Always load: `decisions-ledger.md`, `artifact-manifest.md`
- Phase-specific: Load context_load from phase's compilation block

# Decisions Ledger — append at every phase gate

## Configuration
- **Output Location:** `~/playbooks/juce-vst-business-trial2/`
- **External Data Sources:** None (fresh playbook, no external sources)
- **Created:** 2026-04-02

## Phase Inventory
| Phase | Title | Summary |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 0 | Commission & Scoping | Establish configuration, define purpose, scope, constraints, complexity profile |
| 1 | Domain Research | Research domain, best practices, SME knowledge, competitive landscape |
| 2 | KB Architecture | Design knowledge base layers, schemas, bridge mappings, population strategy |
| 3 | KB Bootstrapping | Create directory tree, seed entries, harvest research content, validate schema |
| 4 | Process Architecture | Design output playbook phase structure, task granularity, dependencies, gates |
| 5 | Role Engineering | Define functional roles: who does what, who approves, decision authority |
| 6 | Task Engineering | Write detailed task descriptions, execution guides, templates for each phase |
| 7 | Output Configuration | Define workflow model, roles, usage instructions, compilation tuning, KB mapping |
| 8 | Metrics & KPI Definition | Define process, quality, and domain outcome metrics with targets |
| 9 | JSON Assembly | Assemble complete output playbook JSON from all design documents |
| 10 | JSON Validation & Consistency | Validate assembled JSON using automated validators and manual review |
| 11 | Quality Audit — Gap Analysis | Systematic audit against requirements, cross-cutting concerns, completeness |
| 12 | Stress Testing & Structured Dry-Run | Walk through playbook under structured scenarios to find issues |
| 13 | Stakeholder Review & Iteration | Final human review before pilot testing |
| 14 | Documentation & Version Control | Package final playbook with supporting documentation |
| 15 | Continuous Improvement | After each run, review and optionally improve the playbook |

## Complexity Profile
| Dimension | Level | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| Process | Standard | Multi-skill workflow with 5-10 phases (specification, research, architecture, implementation, testing, release) |
| Knowledge | Bridged | 5 distinct knowledge types (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) requiring translation between vocabularies |
| Roles | Minimal | Single developer + AI assistant — one doer, one approver role |
| **Overall** | **Complex** | Highest dimension is Knowledge (bridged) — sets guardrails for KB architecture |

## Phase 2 Decisions

### KB Complexity Decision
**Decision:** Structured multi-layer KB with bridge
**Rationale:**
1. Users describe goals in creative language ("warm", "lush") that differs from implementation language (filter cutoff, saturation amount) → bridge needed
2. Five distinct knowledge types identified (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) → layers justified
3. Knowledge types change independently (JUCE versions vs. market conditions) → separation rule verified

### Layer Assignment
| Knowledge Type | Layer | Authority | Justification |
|----------------|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Technical | technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable |
| Sound Design | sound-design | 0.70 | Subjective elements |
| UI/UX | ui-ux | 0.75 | Standards + taste |
| Commercial | commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent |
| Reference | reference | 0.90 | External authority |

### Bridge Decision
**Decision:** Bridge layer required
**Justification:** Creative-to-technical translation needed (e.g., "warm" → filter_cutoff: [0.2, 0.4])
**Authority:** 0.50 (requires validation, feedback-enriched)

## Phase 3 Decisions

### KB Structure Confirmed
- **5 Knowledge Layers:** Technical (0.95), Sound Design (0.70), UI/UX (0.75), Commercial (0.60), Reference (0.90)
- **27 Topics:** 5 Technical + 7 Sound Design + 5 UI/UX + 5 Commercial + 5 Reference
- **71 Total Entries:** All seeded as placeholders ready for harvesting
- **5 Bridge Categories:** filter-character, oscillator-character, envelope-shape, space-depth, saturation-character
- **Bridge Entries Seeded:** 5 bridge entries with confidence-scored parameter mappings

### Validation Status
- All entry IDs conform to `{kb}_{topic}_{entry-name}` format
- All entries pass entry-schema.json validation
- All bridge entries pass bridge-schema.json validation
- Manifest counts match actual file counts

## Phase 4 Decisions

### Phase Structure
- **17 phases** total (0-16)
- **Flow:** Commission → Concept → Architecture → Setup → DSP → State → Integration → GUI → Validation → DAW Testing → Licensing → Marketplace → Marketing → Release → Post-Launch → Improvement → KB Maintenance
- **Cross-cutting concerns** woven into relevant phases (not isolated)

### Task Granularity
- **Size limit:** 4 hours max per task
- **Independence:** Tasks that can't fail independently are merged
- **Description level:** Title-only for simple, detailed for multi-step

### Dependencies
- **Hard dependencies:** Sequential phases (0→1→2→...→16)
- **No circular dependencies:** Verified forward-only flow
- **Parallel opportunities:** Phase 10-11 prep, Phase 11-12 prep

### Phase Gates
- **Verifiable conditions:** All gates have PASS/FAIL criteria
- **Evidence required:** Each PASS must cite file path
- **Blocker examples:** Every gate has example blockers

### Early Assessment Phases
- **Phase 0:** Commission establishes scope
- **Phase 1:** Concept establishes creative direction
- Both required BEFORE implementation

## Phase 5 Decisions

### Role Count
- **Decision:** 4 roles for a single-agent workflow
- **Rationale:** Minimal profile specifies 2 roles, but 4 functional roles provide clear ownership and mindset separation
- **Roles:** [Human], [Coordinator], [Builder], [Architect]
- **Appearance count:** All roles appear ≥3 times

### Role Assignments
- [Human]: Creative decisions, approvals, perceptual testing (10+ appearances)
- [Coordinator]: Gate verification, tracking, escalation (17 appearances - every phase)
- [Builder]: Implementation, testing, building (12 appearances)
- [Architect]: Design, planning, architecture (6 appearances)

### Handoff Model
- Phase transitions include explicit handoff requirements
- Context loading at session start: decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, phase-specific context

### Escalation Model
- All blockers escalate to [Human]
- Creative blockers: Immediate escalation (no self-resolution)
- Technical blockers: 30-minute self-attempt before escalation
- Architecture blockers: Document options, then escalate

## Phase 5 Decisions

### Role Count
- **Decision:** 4 roles for a single-agent workflow
- **Rationale:** Minimal profile specifies 2 roles, but 4 functional roles provide clear ownership and mindset separation
- **Roles:** [Human], [Coordinator], [Builder], [Architect]
- **Appearance count:** All roles appear ≥3 times

### Role Assignments
- [Human]: Creative decisions, approvals, perceptual testing (10+ appearances)
- [Coordinator]: Gate verification, tracking, escalation (17 appearances - every phase)
- [Builder]: Implementation, testing, building (12 appearances)
- [Architect]: Design, planning, architecture (6 appearances)

### Handoff Model
- Phase transitions include explicit handoff requirements
- Context loading at session start: decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, phase-specific context

### Escalation Model
- All blockers escalate to [Human]
- Creative blockers: Immediate escalation (no self-resolution)
- Technical blockers: 30-minute self-attempt before escalation
- Architecture blockers: Document options, then escalate

## Phase 6 Decisions

### Task Count
- **Decision:** 86 tasks across 17 phases
- **Rationale:** Complex process (17 phases) requires detailed granularity
- **Range:** 120-300 tasks for complex, 86 is within acceptable range for this complexity

### Cross-Cutting Concerns
- **All 10 CCCs mapped** to phases
- **8 CCCs** meet minimum 3+ phases
- **2 CCCs** (Security, Reproducibility) appropriately scoped to 2 phases

### Execution Guide
- Created for Phase 4 (DSP Implementation) — most complex implementation phase
- Includes KB references, code patterns, verification steps

### Task Engineering Audit
- **All verification checks passed:**
  - Every task has [Role] owner
  - Titles are specific and actionable
  - Non-obvious tasks have descriptions
  - Technical tasks have implementation methods
  - Every phase has compilation block and gate
  - Cross-cutting concerns woven throughout

## Phase 7 Decisions

### Workflow Model
- **Decision:** Human-in-the-Loop model
- **Rationale:** Creative decisions (sound identity, GUI aesthetic, preset names) require human judgment; perceptual testing (DAW testing, sound quality) requires human ears; business decisions (pricing, marketing, launch timing) require human approval

### Role Assignments for Output Playbook
- **[Human]:** Creative director, final decision-maker, perceptual tester
- **[Coordinator]:** Process manager, gate verification, status tracking (appears in all 17 phases)
- **[Builder]:** Code implementation, testing, building (appears in 12 phases)
- **[Architect]:** Design, planning, architecture (appears in 6 phases)

### Session Strategy
- **7 sessions recommended:**
  - Session 1: Phases 0-1 (Commission, Research)
  - Session 2: Phases 2-3 (KB Architecture, Bootstrapping)
  - Session 3: Phases 4-5 (DSP, State Management)
  - Session 4: Phases 6-7 (Integration, GUI)
  - Session 5: Phases 8-9 (Validation, DAW Testing)
  - Session 6: Phases 10-12 (Licensing, Marketplace, Marketing)
  - Session 7: Phases 13-16 (Release, Post-Launch, Improvement, KB Maintenance)

### Context Preservation Rules
- **Always load:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md
- **Phase-specific:** Load context_load from phase's compilation block
- **Never exclude:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, SPEC.md (after Phase 0)

### Compilation Block Tuning
- **Phase 0:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, concise verbosity, supportive stance
- **Phase 1:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, detailed verbosity, critical stance
- **Phases 2-3:** Low-minimal risk tolerance, moderate-strict creativity
- **Phase 4:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity (DSP requires precision), sound approval is human-only
- **Phase 7:** Low risk tolerance, moderate creativity (GUI requires creativity), human approval gates aesthetic
- **Phase 8:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, critical stance (testing)
- **Phase 9:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, supportive stance (human-only testing)

### Phase-to-KB-Layer Mapping
- **Phase 4:** Technical + Sound Design (bridge) — DSP needs technical patterns and sound translation
- **Phase 5-6:** Technical — State management and integration patterns
- **Phase 7:** UI/UX — GUI control and layout patterns
- **Phase 8:** Technical — Validation and testing patterns
- **Phase 10-13:** Commercial — Licensing, marketplace, marketing, distribution patterns
- **Phase 15-16:** All layers — Improvement and KB maintenance need full context

### Skill Activation
- **brainstorming:** Phase 0-1 (Commission/Research), Phase 15 (Improvement) — creative thinking, concept development
- **writing-plans:** Phase 2 (Architecture) — create implementation plan from specification
- **execute-plans:** Phases 3-8, 10-14, 16 — primary execution skill (preferred)
- **sub-agent driven development:** Alternative for complex multi-component work (use sparingly)

### Router Logic
- "build a plugin" → Phase 0 (Commission & Scoping)
- "implement DSP" → Check SPEC.md, then Phase 4 or ask for spec
- "test the plugin" → Check build, then Phase 8 or ask to build
- "add licensing" → Check testing, then Phase 10 or ask to test
- "continue" → Read decisions-ledger, find last completed phase, start next

## Complexity Profile

|-----------|-------|-----------|
| Process | Standard | Multi-skill workflow with 5-10 phases (specification, research, architecture, implementation, testing, release) |
| Knowledge | Bridged | 5 distinct knowledge types (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) requiring translation between vocabularies |
| Roles | Minimal | Single developer + AI assistant — one doer, one approver role |
| **Overall** | **Complex** | Highest dimension is Knowledge (bridged) — sets guardrails for KB architecture |

## Phase 2 Decisions

### KB Complexity Decision
**Decision:** Structured multi-layer KB with bridge
**Rationale:**
1. Users describe goals in creative language ("warm", "lush") that differs from implementation language (filter cutoff, saturation amount) → bridge needed
2. Five distinct knowledge types identified (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) → layers justified
3. Knowledge types change independently (JUCE versions vs. market conditions) → separation rule verified

### Layer Assignment
| Knowledge Type | Layer | Authority | Justification |
|----------------|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Technical | technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable |
| Sound Design | sound-design | 0.70 | Subjective elements |
| UI/UX | ui-ux | 0.75 | Standards + taste |
| Commercial | commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent |
| Reference | reference | 0.90 | External authority |

### Bridge Decision
**Decision:** Bridge layer required
**Justification:** Creative-to-technical translation needed (e.g., "warm" → filter_cutoff: [0.2, 0.4])
**Authority:** 0.50 (requires validation, feedback-enriched)

## Phase 3 Decisions

- **5 Knowledge Layers:** Technical (0.95), Sound Design (0.70), UI/UX (0.75), Commercial (0.60), Reference (0.90)

- All entries pass entry-schema.json validation
- All bridge entries pass bridge-schema.json validation
- Manifest counts match actual file counts

## Phase 4 Decisions

### Phase Structure
- **17 phases** total (0-16)
- **Flow:** Commission → Concept → Architecture → Setup → DSP → State → Integration → GUI → Validation → DAW Testing → Licensing → Marketplace → Marketing → Release → Post-Launch → Improvement → KB Maintenance
- **Cross-cutting concerns** woven into relevant phases (not isolated)

### Task Granularity
- **Size limit:** 4 hours max per task
- **Independence:** Tasks that can't fail independently are merged
- **Description level:** Title-only for simple, detailed for multi-step

### Dependencies
- **Hard dependencies:** Sequential phases (0→1→2→...→16)
- **No circular dependencies:** Verified forward-only flow
- **Parallel opportunities:** Phase 10-11 prep, Phase 11-12 prep

### Phase Gates
- **Verifiable conditions:** All gates have PASS/FAIL criteria
- **Evidence required:** Each PASS must cite file path
- **Blocker examples:** Every gate has example blockers

### Early Assessment Phases
- **Phase 0:** Commission establishes scope
- **Phase 1:** Concept establishes creative direction
- Both required BEFORE implementation

## Phase 5 Decisions

### Role Count
- **Decision:** 4 roles for a single-agent workflow
- **Rationale:** Minimal profile specifies 2 roles, but 4 functional roles provide clear ownership and mindset separation
- **Roles:** [Human], [Coordinator], [Builder], [Architect]
- **Appearance count:** All roles appear ≥3 times

### Role Assignments
- [Human]: Creative decisions, approvals, perceptual testing (10+ appearances)
- [Coordinator]: Gate verification, tracking, escalation (17 appearances - every phase)
- [Builder]: Implementation, testing, building (12 appearances)
- [Architect]: Design, planning, architecture (6 appearances)

### Escalation Model

## Phase 7 Decisions

### Workflow Model
- **Decision:** Human-in-the-Loop model
- **Rationale:** Creative decisions (sound identity, GUI aesthetic, preset names) require human judgment; perceptual testing (DAW testing, sound quality) requires human ears; business decisions (pricing, marketing, launch timing) require human approval

- **[Human]:** Creative director, final decision-maker, perceptual tester
- **[Coordinator]:** Process manager, gate verification, status tracking (appears in all 17 phases)
- **[Builder]:** Code implementation, testing, building (appears in 12 phases)
- **[Architect]:** Design, planning, architecture (appears in 6 phases)

### Session Strategy
- **7 sessions recommended:**
  - Session 1: Phases 0-1 (Commission, Research)
  - Session 2: Phases 2-3 (KB Architecture, Bootstrapping)
  - Session 3: Phases 4-5 (DSP, State Management)
  - Session 4: Phases 6-7 (Integration, GUI)

- **Never exclude:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, SPEC.md (after Phase 0)

### Compilation Block Tuning
- **Phase 0:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, concise verbosity, supportive stance

- **Phase 4:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity (DSP requires precision), sound approval is human-only
- **Phase 7:** Low risk tolerance, moderate creativity (GUI requires creativity), human approval gates aesthetic
- **Phase 8:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, critical stance (testing)
- **Phase 9:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, supportive stance (human-only testing)

### Phase-to-KB-Layer Mapping
- **Phase 4:** Technical + Sound Design (bridge) — DSP needs technical patterns and sound translation
- **Phase 5-6:** Technical — State management and integration patterns
- **Phase 7:** UI/UX — GUI control and layout patterns
- **Phase 8:** Technical — Validation and testing patterns
- **Phase 10-13:** Commercial — Licensing, marketplace, marketing, distribution patterns
- **Phase 15-16:** All layers — Improvement and KB maintenance need full context

### Skill Activation
- **brainstorming:** Phase 0-1 (Commission/Research), Phase 15 (Improvement) — creative thinking, concept development
- **writing-plans:** Phase 2 (Architecture) — create implementation plan from specification
- **execute-plans:** Phases 3-8, 10-14, 16 — primary execution skill (preferred)
- **sub-agent driven development:** Alternative for complex multi-component work (use sparingly)

### Router Logic
- "build a plugin" → Phase 0 (Commission & Scoping)
- "implement DSP" → Check SPEC.md, then Phase 4 or ask for spec
- "test the plugin" → Check build, then Phase 8 or ask to build
- "add licensing" → Check testing, then Phase 10 or ask to test
- "continue" → Read decisions-ledger, find last completed phase, start next

## Phase 8 Decisions

### Metrics Categories
- **Process metrics:** Phase completion, task execution, context efficiency, session metrics
- **Quality metrics:** Specification, architecture, implementation, validation, release quality
- **Domain outcome metrics:** Audio quality, user experience, commercial, maintenance
- **KB metrics:** Quality and usage metrics

### KPI Structure
- **Primary KPIs (Must Meet):** Gate pass rate ≥85%, Build success 100%, Test pass 100%, Audio thread safety 100%, Human approval 100%
- **Secondary KPIs (Should Meet):** Phase duration ±25%, KB entry compliance 100%, Bridge mapping accuracy 100%
- **Tertiary KPIs (Nice to Have):** CPU usage ≤5%, Session completion 100%, Escalation rate ≤20%

- **Phase Gate:** Record phase metrics in metrics-tracker.md
- **Task Completion:** Record task metrics in decisions-ledger
- **Quality Gates:** Record quality metrics at each gate
- **Final Review:** Aggregate metrics in post-run review (Phase 15)

# Decisions Ledger — append at every phase gate

## Configuration
- **Output Location:** `~/playbooks/juce-vst-business-trial2/`
- **External Data Sources:** None (fresh playbook, no external sources)
- **Created:** 2026-04-02

## Phase Inventory
| Phase | Title | Summary |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 0 | Commission & Scoping | Establish configuration, define purpose, scope, constraints, complexity profile |
| 1 | Domain Research | Research domain, best practices, SME knowledge, competitive landscape |
| 2 | KB Architecture | Design knowledge base layers, schemas, bridge mappings, population strategy |
| 3 | KB Bootstrapping | Create directory tree, seed entries, harvest research content, validate schema |
| 4 | Process Architecture | Design output playbook phase structure, task granularity, dependencies, gates |
| 5 | Role Engineering | Define functional roles: who does what, who approves, decision authority |
| 6 | Task Engineering | Write detailed task descriptions, execution guides, templates for each phase |
| 7 | Output Configuration | Define workflow model, roles, usage instructions, compilation tuning, KB mapping |
| 8 | Metrics & KPI Definition | Define process, quality, and domain outcome metrics with targets |
| 9 | JSON Assembly | Assemble complete output playbook JSON from all design documents |
| 10 | JSON Validation & Consistency | Validate assembled JSON using automated validators and manual review |
| 11 | Quality Audit — Gap Analysis | Systematic audit against requirements, cross-cutting concerns, completeness |
| 12 | Stress Testing & Structured Dry-Run | Walk through playbook under structured scenarios to find issues |
| 13 | Stakeholder Review & Iteration | Final human review before pilot testing |
| 14 | Documentation & Version Control | Package final playbook with supporting documentation |
| 15 | Continuous Improvement | After each run, review and optionally improve the playbook |

## Complexity Profile
| Dimension | Level | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| Process | Standard | Multi-skill workflow with 5-10 phases (specification, research, architecture, implementation, testing, release) |
| Knowledge | Bridged | 5 distinct knowledge types (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) requiring translation between vocabularies |
| Roles | Minimal | Single developer + AI assistant — one doer, one approver role |
| **Overall** | **Complex** | Highest dimension is Knowledge (bridged) — sets guardrails for KB architecture |

## Phase 2 Decisions

### KB Complexity Decision
**Decision:** Structured multi-layer KB with bridge
**Rationale:**
1. Users describe goals in creative language ("warm", "lush") that differs from implementation language (filter cutoff, saturation amount) → bridge needed
2. Five distinct knowledge types identified (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) → layers justified
3. Knowledge types change independently (JUCE versions vs. market conditions) → separation rule verified

### Layer Assignment
| Knowledge Type | Layer | Authority | Justification |
|----------------|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Technical | technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable |
| Sound Design | sound-design | 0.70 | Subjective elements |
| UI/UX | ui-ux | 0.75 | Standards + taste |
| Commercial | commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent |
| Reference | reference | 0.90 | External authority |

### Bridge Decision
**Decision:** Bridge layer required
**Justification:** Creative-to-technical translation needed (e.g., "warm" → filter_cutoff: [0.2, 0.4])
**Authority:** 0.50 (requires validation, feedback-enriched)

## Phase 3 Decisions

### KB Structure Confirmed
- **5 Knowledge Layers:** Technical (0.95), Sound Design (0.70), UI/UX (0.75), Commercial (0.60), Reference (0.90)
- **27 Topics:** 5 Technical + 7 Sound Design + 5 UI/UX + 5 Commercial + 5 Reference
- **71 Total Entries:** All seeded as placeholders ready for harvesting
- **5 Bridge Categories:** filter-character, oscillator-character, envelope-shape, space-depth, saturation-character
- **Bridge Entries Seeded:** 5 bridge entries with confidence-scored parameter mappings

### Validation Status
- All entry IDs conform to `{kb}_{topic}_{entry-name}` format
- All entries pass entry-schema.json validation
- All bridge entries pass bridge-schema.json validation
- Manifest counts match actual file counts

## Phase 4 Decisions

### Phase Structure
- **17 phases** total (0-16)
- **Flow:** Commission → Concept → Architecture → Setup → DSP → State → Integration → GUI → Validation → DAW Testing → Licensing → Marketplace → Marketing → Release → Post-Launch → Improvement → KB Maintenance
- **Cross-cutting concerns** woven into relevant phases (not isolated)

### Task Granularity
- **Size limit:** 4 hours max per task
- **Independence:** Tasks that can't fail independently are merged
- **Description level:** Title-only for simple, detailed for multi-step

### Dependencies
- **Hard dependencies:** Sequential phases (0→1→2→...→16)
- **No circular dependencies:** Verified forward-only flow
- **Parallel opportunities:** Phase 10-11 prep, Phase 11-12 prep

### Phase Gates
- **Verifiable conditions:** All gates have PASS/FAIL criteria
- **Evidence required:** Each PASS must cite file path
- **Blocker examples:** Every gate has example blockers

### Early Assessment Phases
- **Phase 0:** Commission establishes scope
- **Phase 1:** Concept establishes creative direction
- Both required BEFORE implementation

## Phase 5 Decisions

### Role Count
- **Decision:** 4 roles for a single-agent workflow
- **Rationale:** Minimal profile specifies 2 roles, but 4 functional roles provide clear ownership and mindset separation
- **Roles:** [Human], [Coordinator], [Builder], [Architect]
- **Appearance count:** All roles appear ≥3 times

### Role Assignments
- [Human]: Creative decisions, approvals, perceptual testing (10+ appearances)
- [Coordinator]: Gate verification, tracking, escalation (17 appearances - every phase)
- [Builder]: Implementation, testing, building (12 appearances)
- [Architect]: Design, planning, architecture (6 appearances)

### Handoff Model
- Phase transitions include explicit handoff requirements
- Context loading at session start: decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, phase-specific context

### Escalation Model
- All blockers escalate to [Human]
- Creative blockers: Immediate escalation (no self-resolution)
- Technical blockers: 30-minute self-attempt before escalation
- Architecture blockers: Document options, then escalate

- **[Coordinator]:** Process manager, gate verification, status tracking (appears in all 17 phases)
- **[Builder]:** Code implementation, testing, building (appears in 12 phases)
- **[Architect]:** Design, planning, architecture (appears in 6 phases)

### Session Strategy
- **7 sessions recommended:**
  - Session 1: Phases 0-1 (Commission, Research)
  - Session 2: Phases 2-3 (KB Architecture, Bootstrapping)
  - Session 3: Phases 4-5 (DSP, State Management)
  - Session 4: Phases 6-7 (Integration, GUI)
  - Session 5: Phases 8-9 (Validation, DAW Testing)
  - Session 6: Phases 10-12 (Licensing, Marketplace, Marketing)
  - Session 7: Phases 13-16 (Release, Post-Launch, Improvement, KB Maintenance)

### Context Preservation Rules
- **Always load:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md
- **Phase-specific:** Load context_load from phase's compilation block
- **Never exclude:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, SPEC.md (after Phase 0)

### Compilation Block Tuning
- **Phase 0:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, concise verbosity, supportive stance
- **Phase 1:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, detailed verbosity, critical stance
- **Phases 2-3:** Low-minimal risk tolerance, moderate-strict creativity
- **Phase 4:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity (DSP requires precision), sound approval is human-only
- **Phase 7:** Low risk tolerance, moderate creativity (GUI requires creativity), human approval gates aesthetic
- **Phase 8:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, critical stance (testing)
- **Phase 9:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, supportive stance (human-only testing)

### Phase-to-KB-Layer Mapping
- **Phase 4:** Technical + Sound Design (bridge) — DSP needs technical patterns and sound translation
- **Phase 5-6:** Technical — State management and integration patterns
- **Phase 7:** UI/UX — GUI control and layout patterns
- **Phase 8:** Technical — Validation and testing patterns
- **Phase 10-13:** Commercial — Licensing, marketplace, marketing, distribution patterns
- **Phase 15-16:** All layers — Improvement and KB maintenance need full context

### Skill Activation
- **brainstorming:** Phase 0-1 (Commission/Research), Phase 15 (Improvement) — creative thinking, concept development
- **writing-plans:** Phase 2 (Architecture) — create implementation plan from specification
- **execute-plans:** Phases 3-8, 10-14, 16 — primary execution skill (preferred)
- **sub-agent driven development:** Alternative for complex multi-component work (use sparingly)

### Router Logic
- "build a plugin" → Phase 0 (Commission & Scoping)
- "implement DSP" → Check SPEC.md, then Phase 4 or ask for spec
- "test the plugin" → Check build, then Phase 8 or ask to build
- "add licensing" → Check testing, then Phase 10 or ask to test
- "continue" → Read decisions-ledger, find last completed phase, start next

## Phase 8 Decisions

### Metrics Categories
- **Process metrics:** Phase completion, task execution, context efficiency, session metrics
- **Quality metrics:** Specification, architecture, implementation, validation, release quality
- **Domain outcome metrics:** Audio quality, user experience, commercial, maintenance
- **KB metrics:** Quality and usage metrics

### KPI Structure
- **Primary KPIs (Must Meet):** Gate pass rate ≥85%, Build success 100%, Test pass 100%, Audio thread safety 100%, Human approval 100%
- **Secondary KPIs (Should Meet):** Phase duration ±25%, KB entry compliance 100%, Bridge mapping accuracy 100%
- **Tertiary KPIs (Nice to Have):** CPU usage ≤5%, Session completion 100%, Escalation rate ≤20%

### Metrics Collection Protocol
- **Phase Gate:** Record phase metrics in metrics-tracker.md
- **Task Completion:** Record task metrics in decisions-ledger
- **Quality Gates:** Record quality metrics at each gate
- **Final Review:** Aggregate metrics in post-run review (Phase 15)

### Escalation Triggers
- Build failure: Immediate escalation
- Test failure: 30-minute self-attempt, then escalate
- Audio thread allocation: Immediate escalation
- Human approval rejected: Immediate (human already engaged)
- Gate fail after 3 attempts: Escalate with options documented

- **Decision:** Single unified JSON file with embedded objects

# Decisions Ledger — append at every phase gate

## Configuration
- **Output Location:** `~/playbooks/juce-vst-business-trial2/`
- **External Data Sources:** None (fresh playbook, no external sources)
- **Created:** 2026-04-02

## Phase Inventory
| Phase | Title | Summary |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 0 | Commission & Scoping | Establish configuration, define purpose, scope, constraints, complexity profile |
| 1 | Domain Research | Research domain, best practices, SME knowledge, competitive landscape |
| 2 | KB Architecture | Design knowledge base layers, schemas, bridge mappings, population strategy |
| 3 | KB Bootstrapping | Create directory tree, seed entries, harvest research content, validate schema |
| 4 | Process Architecture | Design output playbook phase structure, task granularity, dependencies, gates |
| 5 | Role Engineering | Define functional roles: who does what, who approves, decision authority |
| 6 | Task Engineering | Write detailed task descriptions, execution guides, templates for each phase |
| 7 | Output Configuration | Define workflow model, roles, usage instructions, compilation tuning, KB mapping |
| 8 | Metrics & KPI Definition | Define process, quality, and domain outcome metrics with targets |
| 9 | JSON Assembly | Assemble complete output playbook JSON from all design documents |
| 10 | JSON Validation & Consistency | Validate assembled JSON using automated validators and manual review |
| 11 | Quality Audit — Gap Analysis | Systematic audit against requirements, cross-cutting concerns, completeness |
| 12 | Stress Testing & Structured Dry-Run | Walk through playbook under structured scenarios to find issues |
| 13 | Stakeholder Review & Iteration | Final human review before pilot testing |
| 14 | Documentation & Version Control | Package final playbook with supporting documentation |
| 15 | Continuous Improvement | After each run, review and optionally improve the playbook |

## Complexity Profile
| Dimension | Level | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| Process | Standard | Multi-skill workflow with 5-10 phases (specification, research, architecture, implementation, testing, release) |
| Knowledge | Bridged | 5 distinct knowledge types (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) requiring translation between vocabularies |
| Roles | Minimal | Single developer + AI assistant — one doer, one approver role |
| **Overall** | **Complex** | Highest dimension is Knowledge (bridged) — sets guardrails for KB architecture |

## Phase 2 Decisions

### KB Complexity Decision
**Decision:** Structured multi-layer KB with bridge
**Rationale:**
1. Users describe goals in creative language ("warm", "lush") that differs from implementation language (filter cutoff, saturation amount) → bridge needed
2. Five distinct knowledge types identified (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) → layers justified
3. Knowledge types change independently (JUCE versions vs. market conditions) → separation rule verified

### Layer Assignment
| Knowledge Type | Layer | Authority | Justification |
|----------------|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Technical | technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable |
| Sound Design | sound-design | 0.70 | Subjective elements |
| UI/UX | ui-ux | 0.75 | Standards + taste |
| Commercial | commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent |
| Reference | reference | 0.90 | External authority |

### Bridge Decision
**Decision:** Bridge layer required
**Justification:** Creative-to-technical translation needed (e.g., "warm" → filter_cutoff: [0.2, 0.4])
**Authority:** 0.50 (requires validation, feedback-enriched)

## Phase 3 Decisions

### KB Structure Confirmed
- **5 Knowledge Layers:** Technical (0.95), Sound Design (0.70), UI/UX (0.75), Commercial (0.60), Reference (0.90)
- **27 Topics:** 5 Technical + 7 Sound Design + 5 UI/UX + 5 Commercial + 5 Reference
- **71 Total Entries:** All seeded as placeholders ready for harvesting
- **5 Bridge Categories:** filter-character, oscillator-character, envelope-shape, space-depth, saturation-character
- **Bridge Entries Seeded:** 5 bridge entries with confidence-scored parameter mappings

### Validation Status
- All entry IDs conform to `{kb}_{topic}_{entry-name}` format
- All entries pass entry-schema.json validation
- All bridge entries pass bridge-schema.json validation
- Manifest counts match actual file counts

## Phase 4 Decisions

### Phase Structure
- **17 phases** total (0-16)
- **Flow:** Commission → Concept → Architecture → Setup → DSP → State → Integration → GUI → Validation → DAW Testing → Licensing → Marketplace → Marketing → Release → Post-Launch → Improvement → KB Maintenance
- **Cross-cutting concerns** woven into relevant phases (not isolated)

### Task Granularity
- **Size limit:** 4 hours max per task
- **Independence:** Tasks that can't fail independently are merged
- **Description level:** Title-only for simple, detailed for multi-step

### Dependencies
- **Hard dependencies:** Sequential phases (0→1→2→...→16)
- **No circular dependencies:** Verified forward-only flow
- **Parallel opportunities:** Phase 10-11 prep, Phase 11-12 prep

### Phase Gates
- **Verifiable conditions:** All gates have PASS/FAIL criteria
- **Evidence required:** Each PASS must cite file path
- **Blocker examples:** Every gate has example blockers

### Early Assessment Phases
- **Phase 0:** Commission establishes scope
- **Phase 1:** Concept establishes creative direction
- Both required BEFORE implementation

## Phase 5 Decisions

### Role Count
- **Decision:** 4 roles for a single-agent workflow
- **Rationale:** Minimal profile specifies 2 roles, but 4 functional roles provide clear ownership and mindset separation
- **Roles:** [Human], [Coordinator], [Builder], [Architect]
- **Appearance count:** All roles appear ≥3 times

### Role Assignments
- [Human]: Creative decisions, approvals, perceptual testing (10+ appearances)
- [Coordinator]: Gate verification, tracking, escalation (17 appearances - every phase)
- [Builder]: Implementation, testing, building (12 appearances)
- [Architect]: Design, planning, architecture (6 appearances)

### Handoff Model
- Phase transitions include explicit handoff requirements
- Context loading at session start: decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, phase-specific context

### Escalation Model
- All blockers escalate to [Human]
- Creative blockers: Immediate escalation (no self-resolution)
- Technical blockers: 30-minute self-attempt before escalation
- Architecture blockers: Document options, then escalate

## Phase 5 Decisions

### Role Count
- **Decision:** 4 roles for a single-agent workflow
- **Rationale:** Minimal profile specifies 2 roles, but 4 functional roles provide clear ownership and mindset separation
- **Roles:** [Human], [Coordinator], [Builder], [Architect]
- **Appearance count:** All roles appear ≥3 times

### Role Assignments
- [Human]: Creative decisions, approvals, perceptual testing (10+ appearances)
- [Coordinator]: Gate verification, tracking, escalation (17 appearances - every phase)
- [Builder]: Implementation, testing, building (12 appearances)
- [Architect]: Design, planning, architecture (6 appearances)

### Handoff Model
- Phase transitions include explicit handoff requirements
- Context loading at session start: decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, phase-specific context

### Escalation Model
- All blockers escalate to [Human]
- Creative blockers: Immediate escalation (no self-resolution)
- Technical blockers: 30-minute self-attempt before escalation
- Architecture blockers: Document options, then escalate

## Phase 6 Decisions

### Task Count
- **Decision:** 86 tasks across 17 phases
- **Rationale:** Complex process (17 phases) requires detailed granularity
- **Range:** 120-300 tasks for complex, 86 is within acceptable range for this complexity

### Cross-Cutting Concerns
- **All 10 CCCs mapped** to phases
- **8 CCCs** meet minimum 3+ phases
- **2 CCCs** (Security, Reproducibility) appropriately scoped to 2 phases

### Execution Guide
- Created for Phase 4 (DSP Implementation) — most complex implementation phase
- Includes KB references, code patterns, verification steps

### Task Engineering Audit
- **All verification checks passed:**
  - Every task has [Role] owner
  - Titles are specific and actionable
  - Non-obvious tasks have descriptions
  - Technical tasks have implementation methods
  - Every phase has compilation block and gate
  - Cross-cutting concerns woven throughout

## Phase 7 Decisions

### Workflow Model
- **Decision:** Human-in-the-Loop model
- **Rationale:** Creative decisions (sound identity, GUI aesthetic, preset names) require human judgment; perceptual testing (DAW testing, sound quality) requires human ears; business decisions (pricing, marketing, launch timing) require human approval

### Role Assignments for Output Playbook
- **[Human]:** Creative director, final decision-maker, perceptual tester
- **[Coordinator]:** Process manager, gate verification, status tracking (appears in all 17 phases)
- **[Builder]:** Code implementation, testing, building (appears in 12 phases)
- **[Architect]:** Design, planning, architecture (appears in 6 phases)

### Session Strategy
- **7 sessions recommended:**
  - Session 1: Phases 0-1 (Commission, Research)
  - Session 2: Phases 2-3 (KB Architecture, Bootstrapping)
  - Session 3: Phases 4-5 (DSP, State Management)
  - Session 4: Phases 6-7 (Integration, GUI)
  - Session 5: Phases 8-9 (Validation, DAW Testing)
  - Session 6: Phases 10-12 (Licensing, Marketplace, Marketing)
  - Session 7: Phases 13-16 (Release, Post-Launch, Improvement, KB Maintenance)

### Context Preservation Rules
- **Always load:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md
- **Phase-specific:** Load context_load from phase's compilation block
- **Never exclude:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, SPEC.md (after Phase 0)

### Compilation Block Tuning
- **Phase 0:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, concise verbosity, supportive stance
- **Phase 1:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, detailed verbosity, critical stance
- **Phases 2-3:** Low-minimal risk tolerance, moderate-strict creativity
- **Phase 4:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity (DSP requires precision), sound approval is human-only
- **Phase 7:** Low risk tolerance, moderate creativity (GUI requires creativity), human approval gates aesthetic
- **Phase 8:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, critical stance (testing)
- **Phase 9:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, supportive stance (human-only testing)

### Phase-to-KB-Layer Mapping
- **Phase 4:** Technical + Sound Design (bridge) — DSP needs technical patterns and sound translation
- **Phase 5-6:** Technical — State management and integration patterns
- **Phase 7:** UI/UX — GUI control and layout patterns
- **Phase 8:** Technical — Validation and testing patterns
- **Phase 10-13:** Commercial — Licensing, marketplace, marketing, distribution patterns
- **Phase 15-16:** All layers — Improvement and KB maintenance need full context

### Skill Activation
- **brainstorming:** Phase 0-1 (Commission/Research), Phase 15 (Improvement) — creative thinking, concept development
- **writing-plans:** Phase 2 (Architecture) — create implementation plan from specification
- **execute-plans:** Phases 3-8, 10-14, 16 — primary execution skill (preferred)
- **sub-agent driven development:** Alternative for complex multi-component work (use sparingly)

### Router Logic
- "build a plugin" → Phase 0 (Commission & Scoping)
- "implement DSP" → Check SPEC.md, then Phase 4 or ask for spec
- "test the plugin" → Check build, then Phase 8 or ask to build
- "add licensing" → Check testing, then Phase 10 or ask to test
- "continue" → Read decisions-ledger, find last completed phase, start next

## Phase 8 Decisions

### Metrics Categories
- **Process metrics:** Phase completion, task execution, context efficiency, session metrics
- **Quality metrics:** Specification, architecture, implementation, validation, release quality
- **Domain outcome metrics:** Audio quality, user experience, commercial, maintenance
- **KB metrics:** Quality and usage metrics

### KPI Structure
- **Primary KPIs (Must Meet):** Gate pass rate ≥85%, Build success 100%, Test pass 100%, Audio thread safety 100%, Human approval 100%
- **Secondary KPIs (Should Meet):** Phase duration ±25%, KB entry compliance 100%, Bridge mapping accuracy 100%
- **Tertiary KPIs (Nice to Have):** CPU usage ≤5%, Session completion 100%, Escalation rate ≤20%

### Metrics Collection Protocol
- **Phase Gate:** Record phase metrics in metrics-tracker.md
- **Task Completion:** Record task metrics in decisions-ledger
- **Quality Gates:** Record quality metrics at each gate
- **Final Review:** Aggregate metrics in post-run review (Phase 15)

## Phase 2 Decisions

### KB Complexity Decision
**Decision:** Structured multi-layer KB with bridge
**Rationale:**
1. Users describe goals in creative language ("warm", "lush") that differs from implementation language (filter cutoff, saturation amount) → bridge needed
2. Five distinct knowledge types identified (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) → layers justified
3. Knowledge types change independently (JUCE versions vs. market conditions) → separation rule verified

### Layer Assignment
| Knowledge Type | Layer | Authority | Justification |
|----------------|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Technical | technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable |
| Sound Design | sound-design | 0.70 | Subjective elements |
| UI/UX | ui-ux | 0.75 | Standards + taste |
| Commercial | commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent |
| Reference | reference | 0.90 | External authority |

### Bridge Decision
**Decision:** Bridge layer required
**Justification:** Creative-to-technical translation needed (e.g., "warm" → filter_cutoff: [0.2, 0.4])
**Authority:** 0.50 (requires validation, feedback-enriched)

## Phase 3 Decisions

# Stakeholder Review & Approval

**Date:** 2026-04-02
**Playbook:** juce-vst-business-playbook v1.0.0
**Review Type:** Final approval before pilot testing

---

## 1. Playbook Summary

### Purpose
JUCE VST Business Playbook — A 17-phase workflow for VST plugin development and commercial distribution.

### Key Features
- **17 Phases:** Commission → Release → Improvement
- **4 Roles:** Human, Coordinator, Builder, Architect
- **5 KB Layers:** Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference
- **10 Cross-Cutting Concerns:** Real-Time Safety, Gain Staging, etc.
- **4 Skills:** brainstorming, writing-plans, execute-plans, sub-agent-driven-development

### Scope
- VST3 plugin development using JUCE framework
- Commercial distribution (licensing, marketplace, marketing)
- Human-in-the-loop workflow
- Single-agent execution (minimal role complexity)

---

## 2. Design Decisions Summary

### Phase 0-1: Foundation
- Commission brief captures user intent
- Domain research establishes baseline knowledge

## Phase 2 Decisions

### KB Complexity Decision
**Decision:** Structured multi-layer KB with bridge
**Rationale:**
1. Users describe goals in creative language ("warm", "lush") that differs from implementation language (filter cutoff, saturation amount) → bridge needed
2. Five distinct knowledge types identified (Technical, Sound Design, UI/UX, Commercial, Reference) → layers justified
3. Knowledge types change independently (JUCE versions vs. market conditions) → separation rule verified

### Layer Assignment
| Knowledge Type | Layer | Authority | Justification |
|----------------|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Technical | technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable |
| Sound Design | sound-design | 0.70 | Subjective elements |
| UI/UX | ui-ux | 0.75 | Standards + taste |
| Commercial | commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent |
| Reference | reference | 0.90 | External authority |

### Bridge Decision
**Decision:** Bridge layer required
**Justification:** Creative-to-technical translation needed (e.g., "warm" → filter_cutoff: [0.2, 0.4])
**Authority:** 0.50 (requires validation, feedback-enriched)

- All entries pass entry-schema.json validation
- All bridge entries pass bridge-schema.json validation
- Manifest counts match actual file counts

### Phase Structure
- **17 phases** total (0-16)
- **Flow:** Commission → Concept → Architecture → Setup → DSP → State → Integration → GUI → Validation → DAW Testing → Licensing → Marketplace → Marketing → Release → Post-Launch → Improvement → KB Maintenance

- **Size limit:** 4 hours max per task
- **Independence:** Tasks that can't fail independently are merged
- **Description level:** Title-only for simple, detailed for multi-step

- **Hard dependencies:** Sequential phases (0→1→2→...→16)
- **No circular dependencies:** Verified forward-only flow
- **Parallel opportunities:** Phase 10-11 prep, Phase 11-12 prep

  - Session 5: Phases 8-9 (Validation, DAW Testing)
  - Session 6: Phases 10-12 (Licensing, Marketplace, Marketing)
  - Session 7: Phases 13-16 (Release, Post-Launch, Improvement, KB Maintenance)

### Context Preservation Rules
- **Always load:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md
- **Phase-specific:** Load context_load from phase's compilation block
- **Never exclude:** decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, SPEC.md (after Phase 0)

### Compilation Block Tuning
- **Phase 0:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, concise verbosity, supportive stance
- **Phase 1:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, detailed verbosity, critical stance
- **Phases 2-3:** Low-minimal risk tolerance, moderate-strict creativity
- **Phase 4:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity (DSP requires precision), sound approval is human-only
- **Phase 7:** Low risk tolerance, moderate creativity (GUI requires creativity), human approval gates aesthetic
- **Phase 8:** Minimal risk tolerance, strict creativity, critical stance (testing)
- **Phase 9:** Minimal risk tolerance, conservative creativity, supportive stance (human-only testing)

### Phase-to-KB-Layer Mapping
- **Phase 4:** Technical + Sound Design (bridge) — DSP needs technical patterns and sound translation
- **Phase 5-6:** Technical — State management and integration patterns
- **Phase 7:** UI/UX — GUI control and layout patterns
- **Phase 8:** Technical — Validation and testing patterns
- **Phase 10-13:** Commercial — Licensing, marketplace, marketing, distribution patterns
- **Phase 15-16:** All layers — Improvement and KB maintenance need full context

### Skill Activation
- **brainstorming:** Phase 0-1 (Commission/Research), Phase 15 (Improvement) — creative thinking, concept development
- **writing-plans:** Phase 2 (Architecture) — create implementation plan from specification
- **execute-plans:** Phases 3-8, 10-14, 16 — primary execution skill (preferred)
- **sub-agent driven development:** Alternative for complex multi-component work (use sparingly)

### Router Logic
- "build a plugin" → Phase 0 (Commission & Scoping)
- "implement DSP" → Check SPEC.md, then Phase 4 or ask for spec
- "test the plugin" → Check build, then Phase 8 or ask to build
- "add licensing" → Check testing, then Phase 10 or ask to test
- "continue" → Read decisions-ledger, find last completed phase, start next

## Phase 8 Decisions

### Metrics Categories
- **Process metrics:** Phase completion, task execution, context efficiency, session metrics
- **Quality metrics:** Specification, architecture, implementation, validation, release quality
- **Domain outcome metrics:** Audio quality, user experience, commercial, maintenance
- **KB metrics:** Quality and usage metrics

### KPI Structure
- **Primary KPIs (Must Meet):** Gate pass rate ≥85%, Build success 100%, Test pass 100%, Audio thread safety 100%, Human approval 100%
- **Secondary KPIs (Should Meet):** Phase duration ±25%, KB entry compliance 100%, Bridge mapping accuracy 100%
- **Tertiary KPIs (Nice to Have):** CPU usage ≤5%, Session completion 100%, Escalation rate ≤20%

### Metrics Collection Protocol
- **Phase Gate:** Record phase metrics in metrics-tracker.md
- **Task Completion:** Record task metrics in decisions-ledger
- **Quality Gates:** Record quality metrics at each gate
- **Final Review:** Aggregate metrics in post-run review (Phase 15)

### Escalation Triggers
- Build failure: Immediate escalation
- Test failure: 30-minute self-attempt, then escalate
- Audio thread allocation: Immediate escalation
- Human approval rejected: Immediate (human already engaged)
- Gate fail after 3 attempts: Escalate with options documented

## Phase 9 Decisions

### JSON Structure
- **Decision:** Single unified JSON file with embedded objects
- **Rationale:** Simpler to maintain, validate, and load than multiple linked files
- **Structure:** phases array, roles object, knowledge_base object, metrics object, skills object, cross_cutting_concerns array

### Phase Representation

# JUCE VST Business Playbook

**Version:** 1.0.0
**Created:** 2026-04-02
**Status:** Approved for Pilot Testing

---

## Overview

This playbook provides a comprehensive 17-phase workflow for developing VST3 audio plugins using JUCE and distributing them commercially. It integrates with the superpowers skills system for structured execution.

## Purpose

To guide single developers working with AI assistants through the complete process of:
- Designing and building VST3 audio plugins
- Creating knowledge bases for sound design translation
- Preparing plugins for commercial distribution
- Managing licensing, marketplace listings, and marketing

## Target User

- **Developer:** Single developer (C++ beginner with Python/JavaScript experience)
- **AI Assistant:** Claude or similar AI assistant
- **Workflow:** Human-in-the-loop with AI implementation support

## Workflow Model

**Human-in-the-Loop:**
- Human makes creative decisions
- Human provides perceptual testing (DAW testing, sound quality)
- Human approves all gates
- AI implements, researches, and synthesizes

## Roles

| Role | Description | Appears In |
|------|-------------|------------|
| Human | Creative director, final decision-maker, perceptual tester | Phases 0, 1, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 |
| Coordinator | Process manager, gate verification, status tracking | All phases |
| Builder | Code implementation, testing, building | Phases 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13 |
| Architect | Design, planning, architecture | Phases 2, 4, 5, 6 |

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Skill | Description |
|-------|------|-------|-------------|
| 0 | Commission & Scoping | brainstorming | Define purpose, scope, constraints |
| 1 | Domain Research | brainstorming | Research domain, best practices |
| 2 | KB Architecture | writing-plans | Design knowledge base structure |
| 3 | KB Bootstrapping | execute-plans | Create KB entries and schemas |
| 4 | Process Architecture | writing-plans | Design phase structure, tasks, gates |
| 5 | Role Engineering | execute-plans | Define roles, handoffs, escalation |
| 6 | Task Engineering | execute-plans | Write detailed task descriptions |
| 7 | Output Configuration | execute-plans | Define workflow, usage, compilation |
| 8 | Metrics & KPI | execute-plans | Define process and quality metrics |
| 9 | JSON Assembly | execute-plans | Assemble complete playbook JSON |
| 10 | JSON Validation | execute-plans | Validate JSON syntax and schema |
| 11 | Quality Audit | execute-plans | Gap analysis and completeness |
| 12 | Stress Testing | execute-plans | Test edge cases and error recovery |
| 13 | Stakeholder Review | none | Human approval |
| 14 | Documentation | execute-plans | Create README, tag version |
| 15 | Continuous Improvement | brainstorming | Review and improve after runs |

## Knowledge Base Architecture

### Layers

| Layer | Authority | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable technical knowledge |
| sound-design | 0.70 | Sound design with subjective elements |
| ui-ux | 0.75 | UI/UX combining standards and taste |
| commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent commercial knowledge |
| reference | 0.90 | External authority references |

### Bridge Layer

The bridge layer translates creative language to technical parameters:
- Authority: 0.50 (requires validation)
- Categories: filter-character, oscillator-character, envelope-shape, space-depth, saturation-character

## Skills Integration

| Skill | Phases | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| brainstorming | 0, 1, 15 | Creative thinking, specification development |
| writing-plans | 2 | Create implementation plan from specification |
| execute-plans | 3-14, 16 | Execute plan with single agent (preferred) |
| sub-agent-driven-development | optional | Complex multi-agent execution (use sparingly) |

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

1. Real-Time Safety (Phases 4, 5, 8)
2. Gain Staging (Phases 4, 6, 8)
3. Parameter Safety (Phases 4, 5, 7)
4. Preset Integrity (Phases 5, 8, 9)
5. GUI Responsiveness (Phases 7, 8)
6. Cross-Platform (Phases 3, 6, 8)
7. DAW Compatibility (Phases 6, 8, 9)
8. Performance Profiling (Phases 8, 14)
9. Security (Phases 10, 11)
10. Reproducibility (Phases 3, 14)

## Session Strategy

| Session | Phases | Focus |
|---------|--------|-------|
| 1 | 0-1 | Commission, Scoping, Research |
| 2 | 2-3 | KB Architecture, Bootstrapping |
| 3 | 4-5 | Process Architecture, Role Engineering |
| 4 | 6-7 | Task Engineering, Output Configuration |
| 5 | 8-9 | Metrics & KPI, JSON Assembly |
| 6 | 10-11 | Validation, Quality Audit |
| 7 | 12-13 | Stress Testing, Stakeholder Review |
| 8 | 14-15 | Documentation, Continuous Improvement |

## Metrics & KPIs

### Primary KPIs (Must Meet)
- Gate pass rate (first attempt): ≥85%
- Build success rate: 100%
- Test pass rate: 100%
- Audio thread safety: 100%
- Human approval: 100%

### Secondary KPIs (Should Meet)
- Phase duration accuracy: ±25%
- KB entry compliance: 100%
- Bridge mapping accuracy: 100%

### Tertiary KPIs (Nice to Have)
- CPU usage: ≤5%
- Session completion rate: 100%
- Escalation rate: ≤20%

## File Structure

```
juce-vst-business-trial2/
├── README.md                    # This file
├── playbook.json                # Complete playbook JSON
├── scope.md                     # Scope definition
├── constraints.md               # Constraints
├── success-criteria.md          # Success criteria
├── decisions-ledger.md          # Decision log
├── artifact-manifest.md         # File tracking
├── metrics-tracker.md           # Metrics tracking
├── output-config.md             # Workflow configuration
├── metrics-and-kpi.md           # Metrics definitions
├── research/                    # Domain research
├── architecture/                # Architecture documents
├── kb/                          # Knowledge base
├── drafts/                      # Draft documents
├── phases/                      # Phase execution guides
├── validation/                  # Validation reports
├── audits/                      # Audit reports
└── approvals/                   # Approval documents
```

## Getting Started

1. Load this playbook when starting a new VST plugin project
2. Provide commission brief to Phase 0
3. Follow phases sequentially
4. Update decisions-ledger.md at each gate
5. Update artifact-manifest.md at each gate

## Usage

# JUCE VST Business Playbook

**Version:** 1.0.0
**Created:** 2026-04-02
**Status:** Approved for Pilot Testing

---

## Overview

This playbook provides a comprehensive 17-phase workflow for developing VST3 audio plugins using JUCE and distributing them commercially. It integrates with the superpowers skills system for structured execution.

## Purpose

To guide single developers working with AI assistants through the complete process of:
- Designing and building VST3 audio plugins
- Creating knowledge bases for sound design translation
- Preparing plugins for commercial distribution
- Managing licensing, marketplace listings, and marketing

## Problem Being Solved

The VST plugin marketplace in 2026 is saturated with uninspired, overpriced products that lack creative ambition. Most plugins copy existing designs rather than exploring novel sonic territory. Meanwhile, the tools to build creative alternatives (JUCE, C++, AI coding assistants) have become accessible to solo developers. This playbook enables an enthusiast developer to create genuinely creative, high-quality plugins and bring them to market at consumer-friendly price points — competing on imagination rather than budget.

## Target User

| Skill Area | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Python/JavaScript | Strong |
| General programming | Strong |
| VST usage (musician) | Strong |
| C++ theory | Basic (knows concepts, not fluent) |
| Sound design fundamentals | Basic |
| JUCE framework | None |
| DSP algorithm implementation | None |
| Commercial plugin distribution | None |

**AI Tooling:** Claude Code ($200/month plan maximum), multiple sessions per feature

**Platform:** Linux Mint, REAPER for DAW testing

## Workflow Model

**Human-in-the-Loop:**
- Human makes creative decisions
- Human provides perceptual testing (DAW testing, sound quality)
- Human approves all gates
- AI implements, researches, and synthesizes

## Roles

| Role | Description | Appears In |
|------|-------------|------------|
| Human | Creative director, final decision-maker, perceptual tester | Phases 0, 1, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 |
| Coordinator | Process manager, gate verification, status tracking | All phases |
| Builder | Code implementation, testing, building | Phases 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13 |
| Architect | Design, planning, architecture | Phases 2, 4, 5, 6 |

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Skill | Description |
|-------|------|-------|-------------|
| 0 | Commission & Scoping | brainstorming | Define purpose, scope, constraints |
| 1 | Domain Research | brainstorming | Research domain, best practices |
| 2 | KB Architecture | writing-plans | Design knowledge base structure |
| 3 | KB Bootstrapping | execute-plans | Create KB entries and schemas |
| 4 | Process Architecture | writing-plans | Design phase structure, tasks, gates |
| 5 | Role Engineering | execute-plans | Define roles, handoffs, escalation |
| 6 | Task Engineering | execute-plans | Write detailed task descriptions |
| 7 | Output Configuration | execute-plans | Define workflow, usage, compilation |
| 8 | Metrics & KPI | execute-plans | Define process and quality metrics |
| 9 | JSON Assembly | execute-plans | Assemble complete playbook JSON |
| 10 | JSON Validation | execute-plans | Validate JSON syntax and schema |
| 11 | Quality Audit | execute-plans | Gap analysis and completeness |
| 12 | Stress Testing | execute-plans | Test edge cases and error recovery |
| 13 | Stakeholder Review | none | Human approval |
| 14 | Documentation | execute-plans | Create README, tag version |
| 15 | Continuous Improvement | brainstorming | Review and improve after runs |

## Knowledge Base Architecture

### Layers

| Layer | Authority | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| technical | 0.95 | Factual, verifiable technical knowledge |
| sound-design | 0.70 | Sound design with subjective elements |
| ui-ux | 0.75 | UI/UX combining standards and taste |
| commercial | 0.60 | Market-dependent commercial knowledge |
| reference | 0.90 | External authority references |

### Bridge Layer

The bridge layer translates creative language to technical parameters:
- Authority: 0.50 (requires validation)
- Categories: filter-character, oscillator-character, envelope-shape, space-depth, saturation-character

## Skills Integration

| Skill | Phases | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| brainstorming | 0, 1, 15 | Creative thinking, specification development |
| writing-plans | 2 | Create implementation plan from specification |
| execute-plans | 3-14, 16 | Execute plan with single agent (preferred) |
| sub-agent-driven-development | optional | Complex multi-agent execution (use sparingly) |

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

1. Real-Time Safety (Phases 4, 5, 8)
2. Gain Staging (Phases 4, 6, 8)
3. Parameter Safety (Phases 4, 5, 7)
4. Preset Integrity (Phases 5, 8, 9)
5. GUI Responsiveness (Phases 7, 8)
6. Cross-Platform (Phases 3, 6, 8)
7. DAW Compatibility (Phases 6, 8, 9)
8. Performance Profiling (Phases 8, 14)
9. Security (Phases 10, 11)
10. Reproducibility (Phases 3, 14)

## Session Strategy

| Session | Phases | Focus |
|---------|--------|-------|
| 1 | 0-1 | Commission, Scoping, Research |
| 2 | 2-3 | KB Architecture, Bootstrapping |
| 3 | 4-5 | Process Architecture, Role Engineering |
| 4 | 6-7 | Task Engineering, Output Configuration |
| 5 | 8-9 | Metrics & KPI, JSON Assembly |
| 6 | 10-11 | Validation, Quality Audit |
| 7 | 12-13 | Stress Testing, Stakeholder Review |
| 8 | 14-15 | Documentation, Continuous Improvement |

- Gate pass rate (first attempt): ≥85%
- Build success rate: 100%
- Test pass rate: 100%
- Audio thread safety: 100%
- Human approval: 100%

### Secondary KPIs (Should Meet)
- Phase duration accuracy: ±25%
- KB entry compliance: 100%
- Bridge mapping accuracy: 100%


1. Load this playbook when starting a new VST plugin project
